Canada's unemployment rate was **6.5% in September 2026**. That is **0.6 percentage points lower** than the 7.1% in September 2025.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada Table 14-10-0287-01, vector v2062815.
- **Series:** Labour Force Survey, Canada, both sexes, age 15 and over, seasonally adjusted.
- **Recent trend:** The rate was 6.4% in both July and August 2026, so September was up 0.1 points from August.

**Newfoundland and Labrador** had the highest provincial unemployment rate in September 2026, at **9.1%**. This is the seasonally adjusted rate for ages 15 and over.

- Source: Statistics Canada Table 14-10-0287-01 (Labour Force Survey), vector v2063004, reference period September 2026, released 2026-10-09.
- Next highest: Prince Edward Island at 7.3% (v2063193), New Brunswick at 7.4% (v2063571) and Ontario at 7.0% (v2063949).
- The territories aren't in this table, so I didn't compare them.

Canada's population on July 1, 2026 was **41,798,407**. That is **189,425 people (+0.46%)** more than on July 1, 2025, when it was 41,608,982.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0009-01, Canada, vector v1.
- **Reference periods:** Q3 2026 (July 1, 2026) and Q3 2025 (July 1, 2025).
- **Release:** published 2026-09-23. These are preliminary estimates, so they may be revised.
- **Calculation:** I worked out the growth figure myself from the two published values. It is not a published number.

Alberta grew faster, at about 1.52% against Ontario's 0.28%.

| Province | July 1, 2025 | July 1, 2026 (preliminary) | Change | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alberta (v15) | 5,024,631 | 5,101,050 | +76,419 | **1.52%** |
| Ontario (v12) | 16,216,961 | 16,262,121 | +45,160 | **0.28%** |

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0009-01 (Population estimates, quarterly), released 2026-09-23. The July 1, 2026 figures are preliminary postcensal estimates. The growth rates are my own calculation from the two July 1 values.

Canada had about **2,779,774 non-permanent residents on July 1, 2026**. A year earlier, on July 1, 2025, it had 2,934,388. That is a drop of **154,614 people, or about 5.3%**.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada Table 17-10-0121-01, "Estimates of the number of non-permanent residents by type, quarterly", total for Canada, vector v1566927590. It was released 2026-09-23.
- **Preliminary figure:** Statistics Canada flags estimates from July 1, 2026 as preliminary. Figures from October 2023 to April 2026 have been updated, so the July 2025 number may also differ from earlier published versions.
- **Recent trend:** The count peaked at 2,942,949 on October 1, 2025. It has fallen each quarter since: 2,863,151 on January 1, 2026, then 2,798,649 on April 1, 2026, then 2,779,774 on July 1, 2026.

Canada's consumer price index (CPI) rose **2.1%** on an annual-average basis in 2025.

- The all-items CPI averaged 164.2 in 2025, up from 160.9 in 2024 (2002=100). That works out to 2.05%, which rounds to 2.1%. I calculated the percentage from the two index levels. I didn't pull a published percent-change figure.
- Source: Statistics Canada Table 18-10-0005-01, vector v41693271, reference period 2025 (annual average, released 2026-01-19).
- I took the series ID from the data response itself. I didn't separately check that it is the Canada all-items series, though it matches my recollection of that vector.

This is the full-year average. The December-over-December rate is a different figure and will differ from it.

In September 2026, the year-over-year rates were:

- **CPI-trim: 1.8%.** This is Bank of Canada Valet series `CPI_TRIM`, reference period 2026-09. Its August 2026 value was 1.9%.
- **CPI-median: 1.9%.** This is Bank of Canada Valet series `CPI_MEDIAN`, reference period 2026-09. Its August 2026 value was 2.0%.

Statistics Canada's CPI-median series matches the Bank's figure. It is table 18-10-0256-01, vector v108785714, and it shows 1.9% for September 2026, released 2026-10-19.

I did not confirm the Statistics Canada vector for CPI-trim, so I'm not citing one. I also did not check against Statistics Canada that the Valet series are year-over-year rates. The Valet metadata gives only "Percent", and I'm assuming year-over-year because the Statistics Canada CPI-median series is.

Canada's real GDP was essentially flat in August 2026, down about 0.01% from July.

- **July 2026:** $2,371,788 million
- **August 2026:** $2,371,635 million
- **Change:** −$153 million, or about −0.006%, which rounds to −0.01%

These figures are seasonally adjusted at annual rates, in chained 2017 dollars, for all industries. The source is Statistics Canada table 36-10-0434-01, vector v65201210, released 2026-10-30. I calculated the change from the two published levels. I did not check a published percentage change, so a rounded figure in Statistics Canada's release may differ slightly.

Canada had a merchandise trade surplus of **$4,198.8 million** with the world in August 2026. This is on a balance-of-payments basis, seasonally adjusted, in current dollars.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada Table 12-10-0011-01, "International merchandise trade for all countries and by Principal Trading Partners, monthly." The vector is v87008984, with the trade balance for all countries.
- **Reference period:** August 2026, released 2026-10-06.
- **Recent months:** The surplus was $3,945.7 million in June and $786.6 million in July.

I took the unit from the table's scalar factor (millions). I didn't check the dollar unit separately.

Average weekly earnings in Canada were **$1,354.55** in August 2026, up **$48.12 (+3.7%)** from $1,306.43 in August 2025.

- **What it covers:** average weekly earnings including overtime for all employees, industrial aggregate excluding unclassified businesses, seasonally adjusted.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada Table 14-10-0223-01, vector v79311153, reference periods August 2026 and August 2025.
- **Preliminary:** the August 2026 figure is preliminary. It was released on 2026-10-29.
- **Percentage:** I calculated the 3.7% from the two published levels. It isn't a published rate.

The aggregate that includes unclassified businesses (v1544290282) has no published values for these months, so I used the excluding-unclassified series.

On October 30, 2026, the Bank of Canada's daily average exchange rate was **1.3960 Canadian dollars per US dollar**. That works out to about US$0.7163 per Canadian dollar.

The source is Bank of Canada Valet series FXUSDCAD (USD/CAD), reference date 2026-10-30.

The Government of Canada 10-year benchmark bond yield was **3.78%** on October 30, 2026.

Source: Bank of Canada Valet, series BD.CDN.10YR.DQ.YLD, daily observation for 2026-10-30. The yield was 3.84% the day before, on Oct 29.
